title: 13 Best Herbal Tinctures For Jet Lag
intro: Herbal tinctures for jet lag are liquid extracts made from plants, herbs, and other natural substances that help alleviate the symptoms of jet lag, a condition caused by the disruption of the body's internal clock due to traveling across multiple time zones. These herbal remedies offer numerous benefits, including reducing fatigue, improving sleep quality, and regulating the body's circadian rhythms. Some popular herbal tinctures used to treat jet lag include ashwagandha, which helps reduce stress and anxiety; valerian root, known for its sedative properties and ability to promote deep sleep; melatonin-rich herbs like St. John's Wort and passionflower, which help regulate the body's internal clock; ginkgo biloba, which improves cognitive function and memory; and Siberian ginseng, which boosts energy and reduces fatigue. Additionally, other herbal tinctures such as lavender, chamomile, and lemon balm are also used to help relax and calm the mind and body, making it easier to adapt to a new time zone.

preparations.preparation_desc: Valeriana officinalis tinctures have been traditionally used to treat jet lag due to their sedative and adaptogenic properties, which help to regulate the body's internal clock and promote relaxation. The bioactive constituents, including valerenic acid and valepotriates, work to reduce stress and anxiety associated with jet lag, allowing the body to adapt to the new time zone more easily. By regulating the sleep-wake cycle and promoting a restful night's sleep, Valeriana officinalis tinctures can help to alleviate the symptoms of jet lag, including fatigue, insomnia, and digestive issues. The benefits of using Valeriana officinalis tinctures for jet lag include improved sleep quality, reduced travel-related stress, and a quicker recovery time, making them a popular herbal remedy among travelers.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Praxis", Valeriana officinalis tinctures for jet lag may have a slight impairment of performance during the first few hours after ingestion, but they do not cause significant residual sedative effects or impair vigilance on the morning after, making them a viable alternative to benzodiazepines.

Regular use of Lavandula angustifolia tinctures can help to mitigate the effects of jet lag, promoting a quicker recovery and a smoother transition to the new time zone.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Journal of psychopharmacology (Oxford, England)", Lavandula angustifolia tinctures for jet lag may be beneficial due to their potential to establish a tranquil ambience conducive to sleep.
